claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To start, I need to know about your child or children. 

**How old is your child (or your youngest child if you have multiple)?**

- Under 16 years old
- 16 to 19 years old
- 20 years old or over

This will help me determine which eligibility rules apply to your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm asking about my son Alex - he's 18 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have an 18-year-old son named Alex. This is helpful context.

Since Alex is 16-19 years old, I need to check some additional details about his education or training status. This is an important factor for eligibility when a child is in this age range.

**Is Alex currently in full-time education or approved training?**

For example, is he:
- At school or college studying full-time
- On an apprenticeship or other approved training scheme
- Or not in education/training

This will help me determine his eligibility for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's not in education or training at the moment. He finished school and has been working full-time at a local warehouse.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. So Alex is 18 years old and working full-time at a warehouse, and is not in education or training.

Let me navigate through the eligibility rules based on this information.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to determine which path applies. Since Alex is not currently in education or training and is working full-time:

**When did Alex finish school/leave education?**

- Did he leave education/training within the last 20 weeks?
- Or was it longer ago than that?

This is important because there's a potential extension period after leaving education. Let me get the exact timeframe.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I can see from the rules that there's a 20-week extension period after leaving education. So my question is:

**How long ago did Alex leave school?** (Is it within the last 20 weeks, or longer ago than that?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He left school quite a while ago now - it's been well over 20 weeks. More like six or seven months ago.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex left school more than 20 weeks ago (about 6-7 months), he is no longer within the extension period for Child Benefit eligibility.

Let me navigate to the outcome based on this.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Based on the Child Benefit eligibility rules, I'm afraid I have an ineligible outcome to report:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Eligibility Decision: **NOT ELIGIBLE**

**Reason:**

Alex does not qualify for Child Benefit because:

1. **Age**: At 18 years old, he's in the 16-19 age group where specific conditions must be met
2. **Education/Training Status**: He is not currently in approved full-time education or training
3. **Extension Period Expired**: The rules allow for a 20-week extension period after leaving education if the young person registers with the careers service or armed services. Since Alex left school 6-7 months ago, he is well outside this 20-week window

**Key Rule:**

Child Benefit for young people aged 16-19 requires them to be in approved full-time education or training. If they leave education, there's only a 20-week extension period to maintain eligibility, but only if they register appropriately. Working full-time without being in approved education/training falls outside these criteria.

**Is there anything else I can help you with regarding Child Benefit eligibility?** For example, do you have any other children you'd like me to check eligibility for?

reasonings: Alex is 18 years old and not in approved education or training. He left school approximately 6-7 months ago, which is well beyond the 20-week extension period that applies when young people leave education. Child Benefit for 16-19 year olds requires them to be in approved full-time education or training, or to have registered with the careers service/armed services within 20 weeks of leaving education. Since Alex is working full-time at a warehouse and is outside this 20-week window, he does not meet the qualifying criteria.
arguments.overall_reasoning: Alex does not qualify for Child Benefit because he is 18 years old, not in approved education or training, and has been out of education for longer than the 20-week extension period that would allow continued eligibility."
